field.label: Enable
field.help: Manage the tunnels listed below. Off stops everything on this page and removes the tunnels' firewall pins and MSS clamp; the tunnels themselves keep running. Apply with the plugin disabled stops it, which also removes the IPv6 addresses and routes it maintains.

field.label: Health mirror
field.help: Hold each tunnel down while its WAN is down: the WAN its endpoint route binds it to. Each IPv6 tunnel gateway is held down while its IPv4 tunnel is unhealthy (the IPv6 gateway's own monitor decides the rest). Every gateway change restarts the gateway monitors, and a restarted monitor reads up or down before it has measured anything, so a reading only counts once the monitor has run for the gateway's averaging period; until then the last decision stands. A WAN that is disabled or forced down acts at once.

field.label: IPv6 addresses and routes
field.help: Keep each tunnel's IPv6 address and routes in place: its IPv6 address, next-hop route and IPv6 monitor route (core adds no IPv6 far-gateway route). Off stops maintaining them; a tunnel restart then leaves its IPv6 gateway without routes, unmeasured and reading down.

field.label: Default-route guard
field.help: Keep tunnels from carrying the default route. Removes a default route, in either address family, whose next hop belongs only to a tunnel or another gateway not marked as an upstream (default) gateway. A next hop that an upstream gateway shares is left alone.

field.label: WAN pins
field.help: Keep each tunnel's handshakes on its own WAN. Blocks each tunnel's handshakes from leaving by any WAN other than the one its endpoint route binds it to. Off removes these firewall rules.

field.label: Only NATed traffic into tunnels
field.help: Let only traffic NATed to a tunnel enter it. Blocks any packet entering a tunnel from any address but that tunnel's own, i.e. traffic outbound NAT did not translate to it. Off removes these firewall rules.

field.label: MSS clamp
field.help: Clamp TCP MSS to each tunnel's MTU (IPv4 MTU-40, IPv6 MTU-60), in both directions. It matters on WANs with a smaller path MTU, such as mobile ones.
